title: From Rutherford's nucleus to Bohr's atom
description: The gold-foil experiment reveals a tiny nucleus, and Bohr's energy levels explain why glowing hydrogen gives only a few sharp lines of colour.

sources.title: Rutherford scattering experiments (Wikipedia): Geiger and Marsden 1909 (about 1 in 8000 alpha particles turned back by a platinum reflector), zinc sulfide screen and microscope, Rutherford's 1911 paper, his 'tissue paper' quote, nuclear radius estimate 27 fm and the gold nucleus about 7.3 fm
Plum pudding model (Wikipedia): Thomson 1904, large-angle scattering negligible in his model
Ernest Marsden (Wikipedia): born 1889, a 20-year-old undergraduate in 1909, Secretary of New Zealand's DSIR from 1926, died 1970
Ernest Rutherford (Wikipedia): Manchester from 1907, Cambridge from 1919, Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1908
Bohr model (Wikipedia): published July 1913, energy levels −13.6 eV/n², Balmer 1885 and Rydberg 1888, the model's failures for many-electron atoms, Larmor's radiating accelerated charge
Niels Bohr (Wikipedia): 1885–1962, Copenhagen, the 1913 trilogy, his institute opened in 1921, Nobel Prize 1922 and its motivation
Balmer series (Wikipedia): wavelengths in air 656.279, 486.135, 434.0472 and 410.1734 nm; transitions to n = 2
Johann Jakob Balmer (Wikipedia): Swiss mathematician who taught at a girls' school in Basel; his formula of 1885
Gold (Wikipedia): atomic number 79, empirical atomic radius 144 pm
Fotoni material bank, University of Helsinki: the station on spectra of light sources (filament lamp and gas discharge tubes)
